post.text:
GOING THE DISTANCE. 🧠

The last 24 hours in transhumanism:
- Brain implants kept working up to 7 years in 14 people
- FDA approves Neuralink's pivotal ALS trial
- A protein glue kept old eggs' chromosomes paired (mice)
- A sleepless night left a mark in volunteers' blood
post.alt: A 3-minute video recap of the last 24 hours in transhumanism (27 Nov 2026): 20 years of BrainGate brain-implant data, Neuralink's pivotal ALS trial, Shane Legg's AGI odds, an AI-assisted quantum gravity preprint, OpenAI's AI-designed proteins, people following AI advice they say they'd rather not take, a protein glue for older eggs in mice, senolytics and liver tumours in old mice, waist size and dementia risk, Denmark's no to Kisunla, a blood signature of sleep loss, mindfulness and social media, teen girls' body sense, AI-agent cyberattacks in Switzerland, Australians fooled by AI content, self-assembling DNA cubes, a bionic hand that feels and Singapore's robot district, with captions, sources and screenshots of the articles.

stories.title: Twenty years of BrainGate data: brain implants kept recording for up to 7.3 years
stories.summary: A Nature Medicine study of 20 'Utah array' implants in 14 people with paralysis found they picked up brain-cell signals for up to 7.3 years with only a modest decline, and 11 of 14 still decoded movement throughout. Strong evidence that brain-computer interfaces can last.

predictions.note: Implants in 14 people recorded brain signals for up to 7.3 years: durability evidence for implantable interfaces, still far from two-way symbiosis.

stories.title: FDA approves Neuralink's pivotal brain-implant trial for people with ALS
stories.summary: Neuralink says the FDA approved its LINK Pivotal Study, the first pivotal trial of an implanted brain-computer interface in the US, testing thought control of devices for people with severe paralysis from ALS. Over 30 people already have its implant in early studies.
stories.evidence: Company announcement of an FDA trial approval

predictions.note: A regulator-approved pivotal trial moves implantable BCIs toward approved use, still far from high-bandwidth, two-way symbiosis.

stories.title: DeepMind co-founder Shane Legg now puts 'minimal AGI' before 2028 at about 65%
stories.summary: Shane Legg, who had held a 50% chance of AGI by 2028 since 2009, wrote on X that it's now over 50% likely, roughly 65% for now. By minimal AGI he means an AI that can do the everyday thinking tasks a typical person can.

stories.title: A Stanford physicist proposes a quantum gravity theory worked out with OpenAI's AI
stories.summary: Venkatesa Chandrasekaran's 83-page arXiv paper proposes a quantum theory of gravity built from light cones; several calculations and proofs came from months of back-and-forth with GPT-6 Astra. A preprint that physicists still have to check.

stories.title: OpenAI says proteins designed with GPT-6.2 bound their targets in lab tests
stories.summary: In a preprint with lab partner Onava, 35 of 322 small proteins (10.9%) designed with a prerelease GPT-6.2 bound their targets, at least one for each of five drug targets; a specialist model wrote the sequences. Binding is only a first step toward a medicine.

predictions.note: GPT-6.2 helped design protein binders, 35 of 322 of which bound their targets in lab tests: early lab results, far from an approved drug.

stories.title: People who prefer human advisers still follow AI advice just as much
stories.summary: In three investment experiments with over 1,250 people and real money at stake, most said they preferred human advisers yet took AI advice to the same degree, City St George's researchers report. Disliking AI may not protect us from bad AI advice.

stories.title: A designer protein glue keeps chromosomes paired in eggs from older mice
stories.summary: Max Planck scientists built 'TALhesins' to stand in for cohesin, the glue that fades as eggs age. In eggs from older mice, properly paired chromosomes rose from 47% to 74%, like young eggs. Chromosome errors drive many failed IVF cycles; human eggs aren't tested yet.

stories.title: Old livers fail to clear pre-cancerous cells, and senolytics helped in old mice
stories.summary: In a University of Minnesota mouse study, old livers were slow to clear 'senescent' pre-cancerous cells and only old mice grew tumours. Senolytics, drugs that clear worn-out cells (dasatinib plus quercetin), partly restored clean-up and cut tumours in old mice.

stories.title: Counting waist size as well as weight flags more dementia risk than BMI alone
stories.summary: In British and Chinese cohorts of 18,944 people, a newer obesity definition that adds waist-to-height ratio and conditions like high blood pressure linked obesity to a 93% higher dementia risk than normal weight with no conditions. An association, not proof of cause.

stories.title: Denmark won't recommend Lilly's Alzheimer's drug Kisunla for routine use
stories.summary: The Danish Medicines Council won't recommend Kisunla (donanemab) as standard treatment for early Alzheimer's, citing uncertain benefit and side effects; about 650 people would have qualified. It's the council's second such no in under a year.

stories.title: A sleepless night leaves a telltale molecule in the blood, a small study finds
stories.summary: German researchers found that one night without sleep shifted small molecules in volunteers' blood, with TMAO, made with help from gut microbes, the most promising marker. A small, early step toward a blood test for sleep loss.

stories.title: Mindful people use social media in healthier ways, a review of 43 studies finds
stories.summary: A UCL review of 43 studies and 28,701 people found 39 linked mindfulness with better wellbeing or healthier social media use: less comparing, less fear of missing out, less compulsive scrolling. Mostly one-off snapshots, so no proof of cause.

stories.title: Teen girls better at sensing their heartbeat were happier with their bodies
stories.summary: University of Kent researchers found girls aged 10 to 14 who counted their own heartbeats more accurately were less dissatisfied with their bodies, more so later in puberty. A link, not proof; next they want to test whether body-awareness training helps.

stories.title: Swiss officials say hackers used AI agents in five cyberattacks
stories.summary: Switzerland's cyber agency said five recent attacks on companies and critical-infrastructure operators used AI agents, and that in every case it knew of, the attackers got in. AI agents reachable online have nearly doubled since October, it says.

stories.title: 76% of Australians recently mistook AI-made content for real
stories.summary: A representative survey of 2,000 Australian adults found 76% had recently believed something was real, then learned AI made it. Trust is low (ChatGPT 34%, Claude 17%), and the authors call for clearer AI labels and AI literacy for adults too.

stories.title: DNA cubes build themselves into 3D shapes, like nano Minecraft
stories.summary: Arizona State University scientists designed a 'minimal kit' of DNA cube blocks that find each other in solution and lock into a chosen 3D shape. They hope the method can scaffold future nanorobots and 3D electronic circuits. A lab demonstration.

stories.title: In a Utah trial, a bionic hand linked to the nerves lets its user feel his grip
stories.summary: MIT Technology Review follows a man who lost his hand at 16 and now uses the LUKE bionic arm in a University of Utah trial that connects it to his nerves, letting him steer it and sense how hard he grips. One participant in an early trial.

stories.title: Singapore turns a 50-hectare district into a live test bed for robots and AI
stories.summary: In Punggol Digital District, robots clean, patrol and deliver while one AI platform runs lifts, air-con and waste, part of easing an ageing city-state's worker shortage. The district opens officially next month.

transcript.t: Welcome to the Transhuman Daily, Friday edition.
Let's catch you up on the last 24 hours in transhumanism.
Going the distance!
Brain implants in 14 paralysed people kept working for up to 7 years.
And Neuralink got FDA approval for its pivotal trial, in people with ALS.
DeepMind co-founder Shane Legg now rates minimal AGI before 2028 at about 65%.
A Stanford physicist built a quantum gravity theory with help from OpenAI's AI.
It's a preprint.
And in another preprint, OpenAI's AI helped design proteins; one in nine stuck in lab tests.
In money experiments, people who preferred human advisers still followed AI advice just as much.
On to longevity. In eggs from older mice, a designer protein glue kept chromosomes paired, like young eggs.
In old mice, senolytics, drugs that clear out worn-out cells, cut the liver tumours young mice never got.
And judged by waist as well as weight, obesity went with 93% more dementia risk.
Meanwhile, Denmark said no to Lilly's Alzheimer's drug Kisunla for routine use, citing unclear benefit.
Wellbeing now. In a small study, a sleepless night left a telltale molecule in blood.
Across 43 studies, mindful people used social media more healthily.
And teen girls better at sensing their heartbeat liked their bodies more.
Now, the catch.
Swiss officials say hackers used AI agents in five recent attacks on companies and infrastructure.
Closer to home, 76% of Australians say they've recently mistaken something AI-made for real.
On the frontier, Arizona scientists made DNA cubes that build themselves into shapes, like nano Minecraft.
In a Utah trial, a man who lost a hand at 16 can feel his bionic grip.
And Singapore made a whole district a robot test bed, easing an ageing city's worker crunch.
Implants that last, chromosomes that hold, AI that helps with physics. Here's to going the distance!
Every day, the curve gets a little steeper.
Every day, the future shows up a little earlier.
All of that, in one day. And the days keep getting bigger.
That's the Transhuman Daily for today.
Go build the future. See you tomorrow.
Want more? Meet us in North Sydney tonight.
